desk.headline: Distributable income per share up 12.2% to 192.36c on residential strength and lower finance costs; dividend up 11.5% to 149.97c; 4-6% growth guided for FY2027
results: Distributable income per share rose 12.2% to 192.36c and the total dividend rose 11.5% to 149.97c, while revenue grew 2.6% to R2.23bn.
Residential led: rental income up 6.5% to R594.7m and vacancies down to 6.8% from 8.0%.
Offices remain weak, with rental income down 2.2% and core office vacancies at 25.5%; industrial income fell 6.8% after the Talkar tenant left.
Net finance costs fell 9.4% to R360.4m as borrowings dropped to R4.07bn; 20 non-core properties were sold for R202m.
HEPS rose to 196.66c from 163.36c; EPS was flat at 184.26c after a small property revaluation loss.

guidance.summary: Octodec expects distributable income and distributions per share to grow 4% to 6% in FY2027, assuming a payout of at least 77.5%. It warns that higher fuel prices, inflation and interest rates could strain tenants.

items.metric: Distributable income and distribution per share growth

points: CEO Jeffrey Wapnick said the residential portfolio delivered good growth and non-core sales were sped up.
He said pressure in parts of the commercial portfolio remains a challenge, handled building by building.
The aim is a tighter mix of residential, convenience retail and industrial property with dependable income.
FD Riaan Erasmus said disposals and treasury work improved financial flexibility, and the priority is keeping that strength.
call.source: Octodec results release and summarised annual financial statements, Nov 2026

Office vacancies, at 25.5% of the core office book.
